title: 3D assets
author: mxplr
selftext: So far the dev is going ok, i build a map with Claude, and everything is fine so far. But coming to 3d human model, hand, animation, is another story, i try to use référence, gauntlet loop, tripo3d as well, and all result are crap. When i see others result, even if it's not a good idea to compare, it's night and day.... I've tried to find youtube tutorial, but found nothing i can really rely on. Have you any advise?

comments.author: stream_of_thought1
comments.body:
Building a custom model from scratch will be difficult and expensive, it's easier to edit a preexisting asset. Either ones you make yourselves, or something you buy off of a store (humble, unity store, etc)

It's annoying when Researchingnon YouTube and they say "Claude built custom models from scratch for me" when it most likely just pulled a bunch of free ones from the web.

comments.author: Professor_Snipe
comments.body:
3D asset animation is bound to be very resource-intensive, both time and token wise. At first, getting a decently animated 3D model will take you 2-3 days, which is still great compared to what it used to be like before.

Are you rigging in Mixamo? You can use their animation presets as a baseline too, it is very convenient as a starting point to most animations, unless you need some very special moves.

replies.author: mxplr
replies.body: i tried mixamo, and it was the best i could get

comments.author: Negative_Gur9667
comments.body: I use tripo for the model and I build a motion rig to record myself with 3 cameras for animations. I record the hands separately when needed.

replies.author: s22stumarket
replies.body: Hands? Do you mean wrists and fingers too? With what tool do you capture them? How do you add them to the full model?

replies.author: Negative_Gur9667
replies.body:
You can add them afterwards. I have an old Leap Motion hand tracking camera, but I think with 2 or 3 webcams you can do the same.

I design test scenes for this, an animation suite that starts recording when I shout "go" while the other animation loops.

You can also track your face with a helmet and a webcam on a stick mounted on the helmet.

I also have a weapon with a qr code glued on it.

comments.author: JohnJamesGutib
comments.body:
3D assets are AI's biggest weakness right now and anyone telling you otherwise is either coping or trying to sell you something. To be clear, actually creating 3D models is getting pretty good - Tripo gets quite good results with relatively good topology, for example. But it's rigging and animation that's completely useless right now. Rigging is getting better - animation is unsalvageable. Humanoids can be kinda salvaged by "cheating" and using Mixamo like animation libraries, but actually, truly animating from scratch, not even the frontier AIs can make anything worth shipping. And that's not to mention the horrors of having to salvage humanoid models with fused eyeballs and a stuck together mouth, despite how high quality it can look from the outside.

We still seem to be in the "Will Smith eating spaghetti" phase for animated 3D characters and creatures. Here's hoping it gets a lot better very soon.

comments.author: s22stumarket
comments.body:
The whole 3D animation workflow is a mess. I tried to start somewhere and after 2 weeks noticed that we just do a fix after a fix.

Reverted, made a specific workflow and steps to follow before putting the animations into the game. Still Claude messed up and sayd to me today: "It's my fault. I see these steps in a workflow document but I did not actually check if those steps are implemented somehow."

So, it needs a lot of patience, manually checking the results, tweaking, learning about 3D animations etc. 

All fun.

comments.author: Fault-Content
comments.body:
I'm using trellis2 to gen character model currently, for now I believe the main problem is the designing and steps.

This are my statistics numbers from my jobs:
• Spend: 121.4M Codex tokens over 2,103 jobs since 23 Oct. 68% of the tokens went to judgement jobs.
• Success rate: of 827 steps, only about 20% passed. 405 failed, and 122 came back flagged for review.

comments.author: MidSerpent
comments.body:
For hard surface models, I’ve been getting ok results from ChatGPT + Meshy API, using the T2.5 model only to generate an initial mesh and then having ChatGPT do all the cleanup in cloud instances running Blender.

Only doing the generation is 5 Meshy credits per,  but again this is just for hard surfaces
